repos.name: backnotprop/plannotator
repos.description: The workspace to stay in the loop and on top of agents - shape, decide, plan, annotate, review code, share with team, and send all feedback to agents with one click.
repos.readme_excerpt:
⭐️ NEW: Plannotator Inbox is the missing review layer between you and multi-agent work. It surfaces decisions, prototypes, variations, plans, and everything you need to stay in the loop. Works with all coding agents and personal assistants.

Plannotator is a local, browser-based review surface for AI coding agents: Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Kiro, Droid, Amp, DeepSeek Harness, and Pi. Plannotator Inbox also works with personal assistants (Grok Bot, Muse, Hermes, OpenClaw).

It plugs directly into your agent through plugins, hooks and commands. When the agent proposes a decision, plan, html, or finishes working, the app opens in your browser and you mark it up, comment, and send feedback directly to the agent for it to act on it.

Annotate plans, specs, messages, html, then send the feedback to your agent.

Review local changes or remote PRs. Comment on diffs, suggest code. Your comments go back to the agent. Works with Git, GitButler, Jujutsu (jj), Perforce (p4), GitHub, and GitLab.

For a big change, start a guided review: an agent sorts the diff into chapters, the most important first.

The Plannotator Inbox is one local window where your agents leave you messages, questions, files, and guided reviews while they keep working. Answer a question with a click, annotate a file, and press Send when you can. Nothing holds an agent session open while you do, and your reply goes back to the session that asked.

repos.description: Secure, fast, efficient, battle-tested at Alibaba's scale. Hybrid architecture code review tool: deterministic pipelines + LLM Agent, precise line-level comments, built-in multi-language ruleset (NPE, thread-safety, XSS, SQL injection), OpenAI & Anthropic compatible.
repos.readme_excerpt:
Open Code Review is an AI-powered code review CLI tool. It originated as Alibaba Group's internal official AI code review assistant — over the past two years, it has served tens of thousands of developers and identified millions of code defects. After thorough validation at massive scale, we incubated it into an open source project for the community. Simply configure a model endpoint to get started.

It reads Git diffs, sends changed files to a configurable LLM via an agent with tool-use capabilities, and generates structured review comments with line-level precision. The agent can read full file contents, search the codebase, inspect other changed files for context, and produce deep reviews — not just surface-level diff feedback. Beyond diff review, ocr scan reviews entire files for auditing unfamiliar codebases or directories that have no meaningful diff.

A real-world code review benchmark built from 50 popular open-source repositories, 200 real Pull Requests, and 10 programming languages — cross-validated by 80+ senior engineers (1,505 annotated ground-truth issues).

If you've used general-purpose agents like Claude Code with Skills for code review, you've likely encountered these pain points

Incomplete coverage — On larger changesets, agents tend to "cut corners," selectively reviewing only some files and missing others. - Position drift — Reported issues frequently don't match the actual code location, with line numbers or file references drifting off target. - Unstable quality — Natural-language-driven Skills are hard to debug, and review quality fluctuates significantly with minor prompt variations.

repos.name: ag-ui-protocol/ag-ui
repos.description: AG-UI: the Agent-User Interaction Protocol. Bring Agents into Frontend Applications.
repos.readme_excerpt:
AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications.

Agents don't fit the request/response model. They stream tokens, call tools mid-response, update shared state, pause for a human, and spawn subagents, and every framework does it differently. AG-UI replaces that custom wiring with one bi-directional event stream: the agent emits typed events, and any client can render them, no matter which framework built the agent. The same agent can power a web app, a mobile app, a terminal, or Slack.

Start a new app. The CLI scaffolds a frontend (CopilotKit on Next.js, or a terminal client) wired to the agent framework you pick

Then follow the printed next steps. The generated templates call OpenAI, so set your key before npm run dev

AG-UI is one of three open, complementary agentic protocols. MCP gives agents tools and context, A2A lets agents work with other agents, and AG-UI brings agents to users. A single agent often uses all three, and AG-UI can front agents that speak MCP or A2A. Read more →

AG-UI is adopted by Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Oracle, and built into most agent frameworks. Every framework below has a live demo in the Dojo.

Protocols: A2A · MCP · MCP Apps · A2UI\ Clients: CopilotKit (React, Angular, Vue, React Native) · Slack & Teams · Terminal · OpenBot

Don't see your framework? Build an integration →

Community SDKs: Kotlin · Go · Java · Dart · Rust · Ruby · C++ · Swift

Currently in Beta · Built on React 19+ and StyleX

Docs · Storybook · Sandbox · Contributing · Discord

Astryx is an open source design system that grew inside Meta over the last eight years, where it became the most-used and largest design system in the company — powering 13,000+ apps and shaped by the engineers, designers, and product teams who depend on it every day.

It ships 150+ accessible components, brand-level theming, dark mode, ready-to-ship templates, and a CLI as one cohesive system. You import pre-built CSS and use typed React components — no build plugin, no styling library to adopt — and both people and AI assistants build with the same tooling.

Open internals. Components are built to be composed at any level, not locked behind a closed top-level API. The building blocks you'd reach for are exported directly, and when you need to go deeper, swizzle ejects a component's full source into your project to own. - No styling lock-in. Astryx authors its styles with StyleX, but that's invisible to consumers. Override with className using Tailwind, CSS modules, or plain CSS — whatever your project already uses. - Customize without wrapping. A theme is a set of CSS custom property overrides, so a designer can make Astryx unmistakably theirs without forking or wrapping component source. - Built for people and agents. The API, docs, and CLI are designed together so a person and an AI assistant build the same way, from the same reference.

repos.description: The personal finance app for everyone (by everyone)
repos.readme_excerpt:
The Maybe Finance (archived/abandoned repo) team spent most of 2021–2022 building a full-featured personal finance and wealth management app. It even included an “Ask an Advisor” feature that connected users with a real CFP/CFA — all included with your subscription.

The business end of things didn't work out, and so they stopped developing the app in mid-2023.

After spending nearly $1 million on development (employees, contractors, data providers, infra, etc.), the team open-sourced the app. Their goal was to let users self-host it for free — and eventually launch a hosted version for a small fee.

They actually did launch that hosted version … briefly.

That also didn’t work out — at least not as a sustainable B2C business — so now here we are: hosting a community-maintained fork to keep the codebase alive and see where this can go next.

Sure is a fully working personal finance app that can be self hosted with Docker. Sure can be accessed from a browser, the macOS desktop app, the mobile app, API clients, and LLM agents. See Sure Clients for an overview.

Be sure to include the original AGPLv3 license and clearly state in your README that your fork is based on Maybe Finance but is not affiliated with or endorsed by Maybe Finance Inc. - "Maybe" is a trademark of Maybe Finance Inc. and therefore, use of it is NOT allowed in forked repositories (or the logo)

repos.name: dream-num/univer
repos.description: Build your own AI office with Univer Office SDK. Bring editing, calculation, collaboration, and file processing into your product for people and AI agents. Built on an extensible open-source core.
repos.readme_excerpt:
Univer is an Office SDK for building Office applications inside your own product. It provides Office editing, calculation, collaboration, and file processing for people and existing agents, using your data and permissions. The product family covers spreadsheets, documents, presentations, relational tables, canvases, and PDFs.

Web SDK is the foundation: content models, editing, rendering, formula calculation, and Facade APIs (application-facing APIs). Compose its plugins into an embedded editor or your own Office application, and reuse the content models, commands, and calculation for Headless processing without an interactive editor. - Server SDK adds backend services for real-time collaboration, edit history, and Office file import and export. - AI SDK connects Office capabilities to existing agents and workflows, with content tools, execution, and review integrations.

This repository provides the Web SDK's core architecture and engine implementations under Apache-2.0: content models and snapshot formats, plugin and dependency management, the command system, formula and rendering engines, Facade APIs, UI foundation, and Sheets and Docs editing capabilities. Commercial Web SDK plugins, Server SDK, and commercial AI SDK extensions are distributed and licensed separately.

Agents can use the same open-source APIs; your application supplies the model and tool orchestration. The quotation example demonstrates editing, calculation, and saving without an AI SDK dependency.
